findings.summary: The spike note contains a few minor evidence imprecisions that do not change its API decision.
findings.detail: Independently reproduced the note's core claims against the pinned host asset and jellyfin-web v12.0 source: (1) window.Dashboard is present with the exact method set listed (window.Dashboard=G in /tmp/arrtags-host-dl/host/jellyfin/jellyfin-web/main.jellyfin.bundle.js); (2) Dashboard.showMessage is absent everywhere under the pinned web assets (grep found no matches); (3) alert/confirm/processPluginConfigurationUpdateResult function bodies match the note's excerpts; (4) jellyfin-web v12.0 src/utils/dashboard.js carries the exact 'TODO: Remove once plugins don't need it' comment and alert(object) maps options.message -> dialog text with no .catch; (5) server v12.0 DashboardController.cs line 94 serves the raw resource via File(stream, ...). However three evidence details are imprecise: (a) the note states 'grep across 974 .js files ... zero contain requirejs / define.amd', but three bundled third-party library files do match (libraries/pdf.worker.js, libraries/npo.js, node_modules.hls.js.*.chunk.js); the substantive conclusion (no AMD loader is exposed to plugin pages) still holds because those matches are library-internal; (b) finding 3 says alert(object) 'returns/swallows a promise', whereas the shim returns nothing (the note's own risks section correctly states 'it cannot be caught because alert() does not return the promise'); (c) the evidence field lists '/tmp/arrtags-host-dl/pinned/jellyfin' as carrying an identical web tree, but that directory contains only server DLLs and no jellyfin-web/ (the verified trees are /tmp/arrtags-host-dl/host/jellyfin/jellyfin-web and /tmp/arrtags-14.3/jellyfin/jellyfin-web). None of these affects the recorded availability/stability decision or the 16.5 recommendation, and the note honestly marks the conclusion pinned-asset/source-confirmed, not live-browser confirmed.
